summary.name: Google SRE Incident Management (Adventures in SRE-land)
summary.one_liner: A first-person Google Cloud Blog account of how Google's SRE team handles a production incident, from on-call paging and incident declaration through rollback and blameless postmortem.
use_cases: Learning how Google handles production incidents
Understanding incident commander and operations lead roles
Setting up a blameless postmortem process
Planning safe progressive rollouts and rollback mechanisms
summary.what_it_does: The article is a first-person narrative by a Google SRE who was on a Mission Control rotation with the Compute Engine SRE team. It walks through a real incident: receiving pages, escalating to a primary and secondary on-call, declaring an incident in Google's internal incident management tool, and assigning roles such as Incident Commander, External Communications and Operations Lead. It explains that most production problems come from changes, and recommends progressive rollouts and tested rollback mechanisms, which resolved this incident. It describes the postmortem process, where the tool creates a document, nine follow-up bugs were filed, and reviews are shared weekly, all under a blameless culture. Editor's notes point to related chapters of the Site Reliability Engineering book.
notable: Describes Google's incident command roles adapted from emergency response protocols
Explains blameless postmortem culture with a concrete example
Links each topic to chapters of the Site Reliability Engineering book
caveats: Describes Google's internal tools and processes; the internal incident management tool is not publicly available
Anecdotal account of one incident rather than a general how-to guide
